Lessons.Title: Base-ten Blocks to Divide
ExplanationParagraphs:
Learning goal: You will make sense of base-ten representations for division.
In the previous lesson, you applied your understanding from grade 3 to divide two- and three-digit numbers by one-digit divisors. You worked with dividends slightly beyond 100 and represented your thinking in a way that made sense to them. In this lesson, you work with larger dividends and represent problems with base-ten blocks.

Source activity sequence: Warm-up: What Do You Know About Base-ten Blocks? (10 minutes); Activity 1: Blocks to Divide (25 minutes); Activity 2: Show Us Your Blocks (10 minutes); Cool-down: Division Reflection (5 minutes)
Exact mathematical focus: Divide with place-value blocks; trade larger units when fewer blocks than groups.
Edulytics authored model: Represent 488 as 4 hundreds, 8 tens and 8 ones. Share these among 4 groups: each receives 1 hundred, 2 tens and 2 ones. Each group has 122; 4 × 122 = 488.
First-party Cool-down: Show with blocks how 96 ÷ 4 = 24.
Original diagrams, live construction, classroom response, and publisher login-gated Cool-down are not digitally certified.
